claim: SEC24C colocalizes with LC3B in U2OS cells treated with Torin 2.
source: As shown in Figure 1A and B, a significant increase in the colocalization of SEC24C with LC3B was observed when ER-phagy was induced with Torin 2.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B, which demonstrates colocalization through microscopy and quantification.

claim: SEC24C is delivered to lysosomes during Torin treatment.
source: SEC24C was also delivered to lysosomes during Torin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B), and transport was blocked with MRT68921, an inhibitor of the ULK1/2 kinase that disrupts autophagosome formation (Petherick et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B, and by citation to Petherick et al., 2015 regarding MRT68921 function.

claim: MRT68921 is an inhibitor of the ULK1/2 kinase that disrupts autophagosome formation.
source: SEC24C was also delivered to lysosomes during Torin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B), and transport was blocked with MRT68921, an inhibitor of the ULK1/2 kinase that disrupts autophagosome formation (Petherick et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Petherick et al., 2015.

claim: SEC24C colocalizes with RTN3, but not FAM134B, in Torin 2-treated cells.
source: We found that SEC24C colocalized with RTN3, but not FAM134B, in Torin 2-treated cells (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: RTN3, but not FAM134B, co-precipitates with SEC24C.
source: This finding is consistent with published mass spectrometry data and immunoprecipitation studies showing that RTN3, but not FAM134B, co-precipitates with SEC24C (Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: The long form of RTN3 specifically co-precipitates with the endogenous copy of SEC24C during starvation induced ER-phagy.
source: Furthermore, the long form of RTN3, but not the short form, specifically co-precipitates with the endogenous copy of SEC24C during starvation induced ER-phagy, and only the long form acts in ER-phagy (Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: Only the long form of RTN3 acts in ER-phagy.
source: Furthermore, the long form of RTN3, but not the short form, specifically co-precipitates with the endogenous copy of SEC24C during starvation induced ER-phagy, and only the long form acts in ER-phagy (Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: Mammalian cells have four SEC24 paralogs.
source: In addition to SEC24C, mammalian cells have three other SEC24 paralogs (Zanetti et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zanetti et al., 2011.

claim: SEC24A and SEC24B are 50% identical to each other and closely related to the major yeast secretory cargo adaptor, Sec24.
source: SEC24A and SEC24B are 50% identical to each other and closely related to the major yeast secretory cargo adaptor, Sec24 (Zanetti et al., 2011; Gomez-Navarro and Miller, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zanetti et al., 2011 and Gomez-Navarro and Miller, 2016.

claim: SEC24C and SEC24D are 50% identical to each other, but only weakly homologous to SEC24A and SEC24B.
source: SEC24C and SEC24D are 50% identical to each other, but only weakly homologous to SEC24A and SEC24B (Zanetti et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zanetti et al., 2011.

claim: In yeast, Lst1, but not its paralog Sec24, colocalizes with Atg40 in the presence of rapamycin.
source: In yeast, Lst1, but not its paralog Sec24, colocalizes with Atg40 in the presence of rapamycin (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: The coat outer shell, Sec13-Sec31, does not colocalize with Atg40 in yeast.
source: The coat outer shell, Sec13-Sec31, also does not colocalize with Atg40 (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: SEC24C, but not SEC24A or SEC13, colocalized with RTN3 in a Torin 2-dependent manner.
source: Similar to what was observed in yeast, SEC24C, but not SEC24A or SEC13, colocalized with RTN3 in a Torin 2-dependent manner (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Only SEC24C, and not SEC24A, interacts with RTN3 according to mass spectrometry data.
source: These localization studies are also consistent with mass spectrometry data showing that only SEC24C, and not SEC24A, interacts with RTN3 (Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: Torin 2 did not induce the colocalization of RTN3 with SEC16.
source: Torin 2 also did not induce the colocalization of RTN3 with SEC16 (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), a marker for the ER exit sites (ERES) where secretory cargo leaves the ER (Barlowe and Helenius, 2016; Maeda et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, and by citations to Barlowe and Helenius, 2016 and Maeda et al., 2019 regarding SEC16 as an ERES marker.

claim: SEC16 is a marker for the ER exit sites (ERES) where secretory cargo leaves the ER.
source: Torin 2 also did not induce the colocalization of RTN3 with SEC16 (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), a marker for the ER exit sites (ERES) where secretory cargo leaves the ER (Barlowe and Helenius, 2016; Maeda et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Barlowe and Helenius, 2016 and Maeda et al., 2019.

claim: The RTN3-SEC24C colocalizing sites, induced by Torin 2, are distinct from ERES.
source: These findings show that the RTN3-SEC24C colocalizing sites, induced by Torin 2, are distinct from ERES and appear to be equivalent to yeast ERPHS (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and comparison to yeast ERPHS described in Cui et al., 2019.

claim: SEC24C-RTN3-mediated ER-phagy is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to man.
source: Thus, SEC24C-RTN3-mediated ER-phagy is evolutionarily conserved from yeast to man.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the comparison of mammalian and yeast data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mutant proinsulin Akita is a substrate known to be degraded by RTN3-dependent ER-phagy.
source: To identify and analyze cargo that utilizes SEC24C-mediated ER-phagy for clearance from the ER, we began with mutant proinsulin Akita, a substrate known to be degraded by RTN3-dependent ER-phagy (Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: Akita causes an autosomal-dominant form of diabetes, mutant INS-gene-induced diabetes of youth (MIDY).
source: Akita causes an autosomal-dominant form of diabetes, mutant INS- gene-induced diabetes of youth (MIDY) (Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: High-molecular-weight mutant oligomeric forms of Akita that cannot be cleared by ERAD are disposed of by RTN3, and not FAM134B.
source: High-molecular-weight mutant oligomeric forms of Akita that cannot be cleared by ERAD are disposed of by RTN3, and not FAM134B (Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: In the absence of RTN3, Akita fails to be delivered to lysosomes and large Akita puncta accumulate intracellularly.
source: In the absence of RTN3, Akita fails to be delivered to lysosomes and large Akita puncta, which are thought to be aggregates, accumulate intracellularly (Cunningham et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cunningham et al., 2019 and Chen et al., 2020.

claim: The delivery of Akita-sfGFP to lysosomes is dependent on SEC24C, but not SEC24A.
source: We found that the delivery of Akita-sfGFP to lysosomes was also dependent on SEC24C, but not SEC24A (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Large Akita puncta (≥0.5 µm2) accumulated in cells depleted of SEC24C, but not SEC24A, SEC24B or SEC24D.
source: Furthermore, large Akita puncta (≥0.5 µm2) accumulated in cells depleted of SEC24C, but not SEC24A, SEC24B or SEC24D (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The puncta that accumulated in the siSEC24C cells were similar in size to the large Akita puncta that accumulated in the siRTN3-depleted cells.
source: The puncta that accumulated in the siSEC24C cells were similar in size to the large Akita puncta that accumulated in the siRTN3-depleted cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The simultaneous knockdown of SEC24C and RTN3 did not enhance the accumulation of large Akita puncta, implying that SEC24C and RTN3 act on the same pathway.
source: Additionally, the simultaneous knockdown of SEC24C and RTN3 did not enhance the accumulation of large Akita puncta, implying that SEC24C and RTN3 act on the same pathway (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D, and by inference from the lack of additive effect.

claim: FAM134B targets misfolded procollagens to lysosomes during ER-phagy.
source: Previous studies have shown that FAM134B targets misfolded procollagens to lysosomes during ER-phagy (Forrester et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Forrester et al., 2019.

claim: Approximately 20% of newly synthesized type I procollagen is misfolded.
source: Approximately 20% of newly synthesized type I procollagen is misfolded (Bienkowski et al., 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bienkowski et al., 1986.

claim: Small hCOL1A1 puncta (<0.5 µm2) accumulated in the FAM134B-depleted and MRT68921-treated cells.
source: The smaller puncta (<0.5 µm2) accumulated in the FAM134B-depleted and MRT68921-treated cells (Figure 2E and F), while cells with large puncta (≥0.5 µm2) did not increase in number when FAM134B-mediated ER-phagy was disrupted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Cells with large hCOL1A1 puncta (≥0.5 µm2) did not increase in number when FAM134B-mediated ER-phagy was disrupted.
source: The smaller puncta (<0.5 µm2) accumulated in the FAM134B-depleted and MRT68921-treated cells (Figure 2E and F), while cells with large puncta (≥0.5 µm2) did not increase in number when FAM134B-mediated ER-phagy was disrupted (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: hCOL1A1 puncta did not accumulate in the RTN3- or SEC24C-depleted cells.
source: Consistent with the proposal that SEC24C works with RTN3, and not FAM134B, hCOL1A1 puncta did not accumulate in the RTN3- or SEC24C-depleted cells (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: The small (<0.12 µm2), but not the larger (>0.12 µm2), Akita puncta colocalized with SEC24C.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that the small (<0.12 µm2), but not the larger (>0.12 µm2), puncta colocalized with SEC24C (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The small Akita puncta were associated with tubules and were frequently seen at tubule junctions, as well as the tips of tubules.
source: The small puncta were also associated with tubules and were frequently seen at tubule junctions, as well as the tips of tubules (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Video 1.

claim: Small Akita puncta moved with the tubules as they branched and fused, and some puncta appeared to change in size and shape as they traveled through the network.
source: These puncta moved with the tubules as they branched and fused, and some puncta appeared to change in size and shape as they traveled through the network (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Video 1.

claim: The larger Akita puncta were mostly seen in sheet-like dense regions of the ER and moved more slowly.
source: In contrast, the larger puncta were mostly seen in sheet-like dense regions of the ER and moved more slowly (Video 2, Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Video 2 and Figure 3E.

claim: Puncta movement inversely correlated with size.
source: While puncta movement inversely correlated with size (Figure 3E), no difference in puncta movement was observed in the absence or presence of MRT68921 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: No difference in puncta movement was observed in the absence or presence of MRT68921.
source: While puncta movement inversely correlated with size (Figure 3E), no difference in puncta movement was observed in the absence or presence of MRT68921 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) of the large Akita puncta revealed a fast recovery time (T1/2 = ~13 s).
source: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) of the large Akita puncta revealed a fast recovery time (T1/2 = ~13 s, Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: The recovery of the large Akita puncta was indistinguishable from the recovery of diffuse Akita-sfGFP in the ER network, indicating that the Akita-sfGFP in the puncta rapidly exchanged with the diffuse pool in the ER.
source: The recovery of the large puncta was indistinguishable from the recovery of diffuse Akita-sfGFP in the ER network, indicating that the Akita-sfGFP in the puncta rapidly exchanged with the diffuse pool in the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the FRAP data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The fluorescence recovery of EGFP-hCOL1A1 puncta in siFAM134B cells was decreased (~60%) relative to diffuse EGFP-hCOL1A1 in the network (~90%).
source: In contrast, a substrate of FAM134B-mediated ER-phagy, EGFP-hCOL1A1, behaved differently. The fluorescence recovery of EGFP-hCOL1A1 puncta in siFAM134B cells was decreased (~60%) relative to diffuse EGFP-hCOL1A1 in the network (~90%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Procollagen type 1 aggregates in the ER and shows decreased fluorescence recovery after photobleaching.
source: These findings are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that procollagen type 1 aggregates in the ER and show decreased fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (Ishida et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ishida et al., 2009.

claim: Akita puncta are not aggregates, but behave as liquid condensates.
source: In total, the ability of Akita to concentrate into mobile structures that rapidly exchanged their contents with the ER implies that Akita puncta are not aggregates, as previously suggested (Cunningham et al., 2019). Instead, these puncta behaved as liquid condensates (see criteria established in Banani et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the FRAP and mobility data, and comparison to criteria in Banani et al., 2017. It contradicts the previous suggestion in Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: When ER-phagy was disrupted, the Akita puncta accumulated and enlarged in what appeared to be sheet-like regions of the ER.
source: When ER-phagy was disrupted, the Akita puncta accumulated and enlarged in what appeared to be sheet-like regions of the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Small highly mobile Akita puncta (<0.12 µm2 in size) associated with RTN3, LC3B, and SEC24C-SEC23A in the ER.
source: Here we analyzed three different dominant-interfering prohormones (Akita, G57S Pro-AVP, and C28F POMC) that are targeted to ER-phagy in ER tubules. In studying mutant proinsulin Akita, we found that small highly mobile puncta (<0.12 µm2 in size) associated with RTN3, LC3B, and SEC24C-SEC23A in the ER (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and summarized in Figure 7.

claim: ERPHS accumulated when autophagosome formation was blocked.
source: We named these colocalizing puncta ER-phagy sites (ERPHS; Figure 7) as they accumulated when autophagosome formation was blocked.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data showing accumulation when autophagosome formation is blocked.

claim: Proinsulin colocalized with the ERES marker SEC24A, but Akita did not.
source: Although proinsulin colocalized with the ERES marker SEC24A, Akita did not.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ERPHS, which contain Akita, are distinct from the ERES that target proinsulin to the secretory pathway.
source: We conclude that ERPHS, which contain Akita, are distinct from the ERES that target proinsulin to the secretory pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the colocalization data.

claim: When ER-phagy was blocked, the Akita puncta enlarged (≥0.5 µm2).
source: When ER-phagy was blocked, the Akita puncta enlarged (≥0.5 µm2).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The large Akita puncta resided in sheet-like ER that did not colocalize with RTN3 or SEC24C.
source: The large puncta resided in sheet-like ER that did not colocalize with RTN3 or SEC24C, implying that SEC24C only sequesters Akita into autophagosomes on tubules (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and summarized in Figure 7.

claim: SEC24C only sequesters Akita into autophagosomes on tubules.
source: The large puncta resided in sheet-like ER that did not colocalize with RTN3 or SEC24C, implying that SEC24C only sequesters Akita into autophagosomes on tubules (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the colocalization data.

claim: COPII coat subunits reside on tubules in mammals and on highly curved membranes in yeast.
source: This observation is consistent with studies showing that COPII coat subunits reside on tubules in mammals and on highly curved membranes in yeast (Okamoto et al., 2012; Hammond and Glick, 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Okamoto et al., 2012 and Hammond and Glick, 2000.

claim: The association of SEC24C with RTN3 is needed to target Akita to lysosomes.
source: As the association of SEC24C with RTN3 is needed to target Akita to lysosomes, we conclude that SEC24C is an essential component of the RTN3-mediated ER-phagy pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing that SEC24C depletion blocks Akita delivery to lysosomes.

claim: SEC24C is an essential component of the RTN3-mediated ER-phagy pathway.
source: As the association of SEC24C with RTN3 is needed to target Akita to lysosomes, we conclude that SEC24C is an essential component of the RTN3-mediated ER-phagy pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: ERAD-resistant high-molecular-weight oligomeric forms of Akita are cleared from the ER by RTN3.
source: Previous studies have shown that ERAD-resistant high-molecular-weight oligomeric forms of Akita are cleared from the ER by RTN3 (Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: Akita oligomers pelleted on sucrose density gradients and were suggested to be aggregates.
source: Because these oligomers pelleted on sucrose density gradients, they were suggested to be aggregates (Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: Condensates have not been observed within the ER before.
source: Our photobleach analysis of Akita puncta, showing that these structures behaved like liquid condensates and not aggregates, was surprising as condensates have not been observed within the ER before.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: ER tubules play a critical role in restricting the size of condensates in the ER.
source: This observation led us to discover that ER tubules play a critical role in restricting the size of condensates in the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing that loss of tubules leads to enlarged puncta.

claim: The loss of ER tubules in LNPK KO cells resulted in a dramatic accumulation of large Akita puncta (≥0.5 µm2).
source: Specifically, we found that the loss of ER tubules in LNPK KO cells resulted in a dramatic accumulation of large Akita puncta (≥0.5 µm2; Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and summarized in Figure 7.

claim: The Akita puncta not only failed to be degraded in the absence of tubules, they continued to enlarge.
source: The puncta not only failed to be degraded in the absence of tubules, they continued to enlarge (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and summarized in Figure 7.

claim: The overexpression of RTN4 partially restored the tubular network in LNPK KO cells and reduced the number of large puncta.
source: The overexpression of RTN4, a protein that promotes tubule formation, partially restored the tubular network in LNPK KO cells and reduced the number of large puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: RTN4 overexpression increased the delivery of Akita to lysosomes.
source: RTN4 overexpression also increased the delivery of Akita to lysosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The proliferation of ER sheets by CLIMP63 overexpression increased the number of large Akita puncta and reduced the delivery of Akita to lysosomes.
source: Consistent with the proposal that the Akita puncta enlarged in sheet-like ER, and not tubules, the proliferation of ER sheets by CLIMP63 overexpression increased the number of large Akita puncta and reduced the delivery of Akita to lysosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The co-transfection of CLIMP63 with RTN4 restored the tubular network in the CLIMP63-overexpressing cells and reduced the number of large Akita puncta.
source: The co-transfection of CLIMP63 with RTN4 restored the tubular network in the CLIMP63-overexpressing cells and reduced the number of large Akita puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ER tubules, which have a small outer radius of only ~44 nm, restrict the size of condensates.
source: In total, these findings indicate that ER tubules, which have a small outer radius of only ~44 nm (Georgiades et al., 2017), restrict the size of condensates.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citation to Georgiades et al., 2017 for the tubule radius.

claim: In a sheet, an Akita condensate can access the soluble milieu around its entire surface, while in a tubule, accessibility is limited to the ends facing the lumen.
source: In a sheet, an Akita condensate can access the soluble milieu around its entire surface, while in a tubule, accessibility is limited to the ends facing the lumen.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the geometry of sheets and tubules.

claim: An Akita condensate is inaccessible to soluble oligomers in the area that is adjacent to the tubule wall.
source: An Akita condensate is inaccessible to soluble oligomers in the area that is adjacent to the tubule wall.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the geometry of tubules.

claim: Although Akita condensates could expand along the length of tubules, their growth rate is limited by their reduced accessibility.
source: Therefore, although Akita condensates could expand along the length of tubules, their growth rate is limited by their reduced accessibility.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the geometry of tubules and the accessibility argument.

claim: Other RTN3-SEC24C substrates (G57S Pro-AVP and C28F POMC) behaved like Akita.
source: Interestingly, other RTN3-SEC24C substrates (G57S Pro-AVP and C28F POMC) behaved like Akita, while a cargo that is targeted for lysosomal degradation in the sheets (hCOL1A1) did not.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A cargo that is targeted for lysosomal degradation in the sheets (hCOL1A1) did not behave like Akita.
source: Interestingly, other RTN3-SEC24C substrates (G57S Pro-AVP and C28F POMC) behaved like Akita, while a cargo that is targeted for lysosomal degradation in the sheets (hCOL1A1) did not.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Misfolded proteins, which form fluid condensates, are largely disposed of by ER-phagy in tubules.
source: Together these findings imply that misfolded proteins, which form fluid condensates, are largely disposed of by ER-phagy in tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Unlike aggregates, which are biologically inert, condensates have the ability to rapidly exchange their contents with the surrounding environment.
source: Unlike aggregates, which are biologically inert, condensates have the ability to rapidly exchange their contents with the surrounding environment (Banani et al., 2017; Noda et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Banani et al., 2017 and Noda et al., 2020.

claim: FRAP studies showing that Akita in puncta rapidly exchanged with Akita in the ER provide a possible explanation for how Akita can trap secretory cargo and disrupt the local environment of the ER.
source: Our FRAP studies showing that Akita in puncta rapidly exchanged with Akita in the ER provide a possible explanation for how Akita can trap secretory cargo and disrupt the local environment of the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the FRAP data.

claim: A comparison of the toxicity of liquid and aggregated states of α-synuclein has suggested that soluble oligomers of mutant α-synuclein, and not aggregated forms, are the toxic species in Parkinson disease.
source: Consistent with our findings, a comparison of the toxicity of liquid and aggregated states of α-synuclein has suggested that soluble oligomers of mutant α-synuclein, and not aggregated forms, are the toxic species in Parkinson disease (Winner et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Winner et al., 2011.

claim: In Alzheimer's disease, soluble Aβ oligomers and not amyloid fibrils have been shown to be neurotoxic.
source: Similarly, in Alzheimer's disease, soluble Aβ oligomers and not amyloid fibrils have been shown to be neurotoxic (Walsh et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Walsh et al., 2002.

claim: ER-phagy is induced slowly.
source: As ER-phagy is induced slowly (Cui et al., 2019), misfolded cargoes can accumulate in the ER before they are removed.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: The ability of tubules to restrict condensate size averts potentially toxic condensates from expanding in the ER while they are waiting to undergo ER-phagy.
source: The ability of tubules to restrict condensate size averts potentially toxic condensates from expanding in the ER while they are waiting to undergo ER-phagy.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and the proposed mechanism.

claim: Drugs that reduce the size of Akita puncta in the ER could be of therapeutic value in the intervention of MIDY.
source: In total, our findings suggest that drugs that reduce the size of Akita puncta in the ER could be of therapeutic value in the intervention of MIDY.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation from the findings.

claim: The observations made here can be extended to a variety of other disorders that are associated with the accumulation of dominant-interfering, ERAD-resistant proteins in the ER.
source: We also speculate that the observations we have made here can be extended to a variety of other disorders that are associated with the accumulation of dominant-interfering, ERAD-resistant proteins in the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation from the findings.

claim: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) forms a continuous polygonal network of interconnected sheets and tubules that extends from the nucleus to the cell periphery.
source: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) forms a continuous polygonal network of interconnected sheets and tubules that extends from the nucleus to the cell periphery (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2013.

claim: ER shape is dependent on the reticulons (RTN), atlastin (ATL), and lunapark (LNPK) proteins.
source: ER shape is dependent on the reticulons (RTN), atlastin (ATL), and lunapark (LNPK) proteins (Voeltz et al., 2006; De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Orso et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Voeltz et al., 2006; De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Orso et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2015.

claim: The reticulons are required to stabilize tubules.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Voeltz et al., 2006; De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Orso et al., 2009.

claim: The atlastins mediate tubule-tubule fusion.
source: The reticulons are required to stabilize tubules, while the atlastins mediate tubule-tubule fusion (Voeltz et al., 2006; De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Orso et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Voeltz et al., 2006; De Craene et al., 2006; Hu et al., 2009; Orso et al., 2009.

claim: LNPK resides at the junctions formed when two tubules fuse and regulates ER architecture by stabilizing nascent tubule junctions.
source: LNPK, which resides at the junctions formed when two tubules fuse, regulates ER architecture by stabilizing nascent tubule junctions (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: In the absence of LNPK, ER junctions are destabilized, and as a consequence, the tubular network collapses.
source: In the absence of LNPK, ER junctions are destabilized, and as a consequence, the tubular network collapses (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: Mutations in ER-shaping proteins have been associated with neurodegenerative disorders, such as hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy and hereditary spastic paraplegias.
source: ER network organization may be important for cell health as mutations in ER-shaping proteins have been associated with neurodegenerative disorders, such as hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy and hereditary spastic paraplegias (Zhang and Hu, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zhang and Hu, 2016.

claim: When errors in protein processing, protein folding, and protein complex assembly occur, ER proteostasis is disrupted and aberrant proteins accumulate in the ER.
source: When errors in protein processing, protein folding, and protein complex assembly occur, ER proteostasis is disrupted and aberrant proteins accumulate in the ER (Sun and Brodsky, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sun and Brodsky, 2019.

claim: Cells use two major degradative mechanisms to restore homeostasis, the proteasome and autophagy.
source: Cells use two major degradative mechanisms to restore homeostasis, the proteasome and autophagy (Sun and Brodsky, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sun and Brodsky, 2019.

claim: Misfolded ER proteins can be retrotranslocated across the membrane into the cytosol by the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) machinery where they are degraded by the proteasome.
source: Misfolded ER proteins can be retrotranslocated across the membrane into the cytosol by the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) machinery where they are degraded by the proteasome (Sun and Brodsky, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sun and Brodsky, 2019.

claim: Some misfolded proteins are resistant to ERAD and must use other disposal pathways.
source: Some misfolded proteins, however, are resistant to ERAD and must use other disposal pathways (Sun and Brodsky, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sun and Brodsky, 2019.

claim: Autophagy is an alternate pathway that degrades organelles, pathogens, protein aggregates, and liquid protein condensates.
source: Autophagy is an alternate pathway that degrades organelles, pathogens, protein aggregates, and liquid protein condensates (Mizushima et al., 2011; Yamasaki et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mizushima et al., 2011 and Yamasaki et al., 2020.

claim: ER autophagy (termed ER-phagy) is a type of selective autophagy that targets a domain of the ER to the lysosome for degradation.
source: ER autophagy (termed ER-phagy) is a type of selective autophagy that targets a domain of the ER to the lysosome for degradation (Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021.

claim: ER to lysosome degradation occurs via a double membrane vesicle called the autophagosome (macro-ER-phagy) or can be non-autophagosome mediated.
source: ER to lysosome degradation occurs via a double membrane vesicle called the autophagosome (macro-ER-phagy) or can be non-autophagosome mediated (Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021.

claim: ER-phagy uses receptors that connect the ER to the autophagy machinery via their ability to bind Atg8 in yeast or LC3 or GABARAP in mammals.
source: ER-phagy uses receptors that connect the ER to the autophagy machinery via their ability to bind Atg8 in yeast or LC3 or GABARAP in mammals (Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fregno and Molinari, 2019; Wilkinson, 2020; Chino and Mizushima, 2020; Hübner and Dikic, 2020; Ferro-Novick et al., 2021.

claim: Two ER-phagy membrane receptors have been identified in yeast and six in mammals.
source: To date, two ER-phagy membrane receptors have been identified in yeast and six in mammals.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of the field.

claim: Several soluble ER-phagy receptors have recently been reported.
source: Additionally, several soluble receptors have recently been reported (Ferro-Novick et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ferro-Novick et al., 2021.

claim: Different membrane ER-phagy receptors mark the distinct morphological domains of the ER.
source: Different membrane ER-phagy receptors mark the distinct morphological domains of the ER.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of the field.

claim: In mammals, the autophagy receptor FAM134B resides in the curved edges of ER sheets.
source: For example, in mammals, the autophagy receptor FAM134B resides in the curved edges of ER sheets, while the long form of the ER-phagy receptor RTN3 (herein called RTN3) localizes to the tubular ER (Khaminets et al., 2015; Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khaminets et al., 2015 and Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: The long form of the ER-phagy receptor RTN3 localizes to the tubular ER.
source: For example, in mammals, the autophagy receptor FAM134B resides in the curved edges of ER sheets, while the long form of the ER-phagy receptor RTN3 (herein called RTN3) localizes to the tubular ER (Khaminets et al., 2015; Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khaminets et al., 2015 and Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: FAM134B and RTN3 are required for ER proteostasis.
source: Recent studies have revealed that FAM134B and RTN3 are required for ER proteostasis (Forrester et al., 2019; Schultz et al., 2018; Fregno et al., 2018; Cunningham et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Forrester et al., 2019; Schultz et al., 2018; Fregno et al., 2018; Cunningham et al., 2019.

claim: FAM134B and RTN3 contain reticulon homology domains that generate regions of high membrane curvature and have ER fragmenting activity.
source: These receptors contain reticulon homology domains that generate regions of high membrane curvature and have ER fragmenting activity (Khaminets et al., 2015; Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khaminets et al., 2015 and Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: The delivery of ER tubules to lysosomes during ER-phagy requires SEC24C in mammals and Lst1 in yeast.
source: The delivery of ER tubules to lysosomes during ER-phagy also requires SEC24C in mammals and Lst1 in yeast (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: SEC24C, and its homologue Lst1, are COPII coat cargo adaptors that sort proteins into ER-derived transport carriers that traffic to the Golgi.
source: SEC24C, and its homologue Lst1, are COPII coat cargo adaptors that sort proteins into ER-derived transport carriers that traffic to the Golgi (Zanetti et al., 2011; Gomez-Navarro and Miller, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zanetti et al., 2011 and Gomez-Navarro and Miller, 2016.

claim: Mutant proinsulin Akita, misfolded prohormone pro-opiomelanocortin (C28F POMC), and the mutant neuropeptide pro-arginine-vasopressin (G57S Pro-AVP) are dominant-interfering disease-causing proteins that are segregated into tubules before undergoing ER-phagy.
source: For our studies, we analyzed mutant proinsulin Akita, as well as misfolded prohormone pro-opiomelanocortin (C28F POMC) and the mutant neuropeptide pro-arginine-vasopressin (G57S Pro-AVP). All three cargoes are dominant-interfering disease-causing proteins that are segregated into tubules before undergoing ER-phagy.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: When autophagy is induced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae with the TORC1 kinase inhibitor, rapamycin, Lst1 associates with Atg8 and Atg40 to facilitate the packaging of ER into autophagosomes.
source: We previously showed that when autophagy is induced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae with the TORC1 kinase inhibitor, rapamycin, Lst1 associates with Atg8 and Atg40 to facilitate the packaging of ER into autophagosomes (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: The sites on the ER where Lst1 colocalizes with the autophagy machinery are named ER-phagy sites (ERPHS).
source: We named the sites on the ER where Lst1 colocalizes with the autophagy machinery ER-phagy sites (ERPHS) (Cui et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Cui et al., 2019.

claim: The small Akita puncta preferentially colocalized with SEC24C, and not SEC24A.
source: We found that the small Akita puncta preferentially colocalized with SEC24C, and not SEC24A (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The binding partner for all SEC24 isoforms, SEC23A, also colocalized with Akita.
source: The binding partner for all SEC24 isoforms, SEC23A, also colocalized with Akita (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: A juxtanuclear pool of proinsulin was observed.
source: Consistent with published localization studies, we observed a juxtanuclear pool of proinsulin (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A; Haataja et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and citation to Haataja et al., 2013.

claim: The juxtanuclear steady-state pool of proinsulin was previously shown to colocalize with the early Golgi marker p115 in U2OS cells.
source: The juxtanuclear steady-state pool was previously shown to colocalize with the early Golgi marker p115 in U2OS cells (Haataja et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Haataja et al., 2013.

claim: Proinsulin was observed on ER tubules and on puncta that colocalize with the ERES marker, SEC24A.
source: Additionally, we also observed proinsulin on ER tubules and on puncta that colocalize with the ERES marker, SEC24A (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Proinsulin puncta colocalized equally as well with SEC24A and SEC24C.
source: In contrast to what we observed for Akita, proinsulin puncta colocalized equally as well with SEC24A and SEC24C (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B ).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The proinsulin puncta that colocalized with SEC24A appeared to be similar in size to the Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24C.
source: Interestingly, the proinsulin puncta that colocalized with SEC24A appeared to be similar in size to the Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24C (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: A dramatic increase in the percent of cells with multiple Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24C was observed in the presence of MRT68921.
source: A dramatic increase in the percent of cells with multiple Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24C was observed in the presence of inhibitor, while no significant increase was found for SEC24A (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: No significant increase in the percent of cells with multiple Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24A was found in the presence of MRT68921.
source: A dramatic increase in the percent of cells with multiple Akita puncta that colocalized with SEC24C was observed in the presence of inhibitor, while no significant increase was found for SEC24A (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The increased colocalization of Akita with SEC24C, observed during treatment with MRT68921, was dependent on RTN3.
source: The increased colocalization of Akita with SEC24C, observed during treatment with MRT68921, was dependent on RTN3 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The number of cells with multiple Akita puncta colocalizing with LC3B increased in the presence of MRT68921.
source: When we analyzed the localization of LC3B, a known binding partner for RTN3 (Grumati et al., 2017), the number of cells with multiple Akita puncta colocalizing with LC3B also increased in the presence of MRT68921 (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E, and citation to Grumati et al., 2017 regarding LC3B as a binding partner for RTN3.

claim: LC3B is a known binding partner for RTN3.
source: When we analyzed the localization of LC3B, a known binding partner for RTN3 (Grumati et al., 2017), the number of cells with multiple Akita puncta colocalizing with LC3B also increased in the presence of MRT68921 (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: The increase in cells with multiple Akita puncta colocalizing with LC3B was dependent on RTN3.
source: Additionally, this increase was dependent on RTN3 (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Akita puncta still colocalized with LC3B in the absence of SEC24C.
source: Akita puncta still colocalized with LC3B in the absence of SEC24C (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C and D), indicating that the association of RTN3 with LC3B does not depend on SEC24C.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: The association of RTN3 with LC3B does not depend on SEC24C.
source: Akita puncta still colocalized with LC3B in the absence of SEC24C (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C and D), indicating that the association of RTN3 with LC3B does not depend on SEC24C.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: Small Akita puncta that associate with RTN3, LC3B, and SEC24C form ERPHS on ER tubules.
source: In total, these studies imply that small Akita puncta that associate with RTN3, LC3B, and SEC24C form ERPHS on ER tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: In the absence of LNPK, fewer junctions are observed and the tubular network collapses.
source: In the absence of LNPK, fewer junctions are observed and the tubular network collapses (Chen et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2012 and Chen et al., 2015.

claim: The loss of tubules in the LNPK knock-out (KO) cells shifts the morphology of the ER to a more sheet-like network.
source: The loss of tubules in the knock-out (KO) cells shifts the morphology of the ER to a more sheet-like network (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2015.

claim: ~76% of the LNPK KO cells contained large Akita puncta.
source: We found that ~76% of the LNPK KO cells contained large puncta (Figure 5A), while ~15% of the control cells and ~45% of the siRTN3 and siSEC24C-depleted cells contained large puncta (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ~15% of the control cells contained large Akita puncta.
source: We found that ~76% of the LNPK KO cells contained large puncta (Figure 5A), while ~15% of the control cells and ~45% of the siRTN3 and siSEC24C-depleted cells contained large puncta (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: ~45% of the siRTN3 and siSEC24C-depleted cells contained large Akita puncta.
source: We found that ~76% of the LNPK KO cells contained large puncta (Figure 5A), while ~15% of the control cells and ~45% of the siRTN3 and siSEC24C-depleted cells contained large puncta (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A large fraction (~35%) of the LNPK KO cells contained multiple large Akita puncta.
source: A large fraction (~35%) of the LNPK KO cells (Figure 5A) also contained multiple large puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 3D reconstructions of deconvolved Z stacks verified that the small Akita puncta reside in tubules, while the large puncta are in ER sheets.
source: To examine the Akita puncta in more detail, we analyzed 3D reconstructions of deconvolved Z stacks of control and LNPK KO cells (see representative Videos 3 and 4, and frames in Figure 5B and C). This analysis verified that the small puncta reside in tubules, while the large puncta are in ER sheets.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Videos 3 and 4, and Figure 5B and C.

claim: ER sheet proliferation, which was induced by CLIMP63 overexpression, increased the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta.
source: ER sheet proliferation, which was induced by CLIMP63 overexpression, increased the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D, Video 5), as well as the mean size of Akita puncta per cell (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D and Video 5.

claim: CLIMP63 overexpression increased the mean size of Akita puncta per cell.
source: ER sheet proliferation, which was induced by CLIMP63 overexpression, increased the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D, Video 5), as well as the mean size of Akita puncta per cell (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: A similar increase in the mean size of Akita puncta per cell was observed in LNPK KO cells.
source: A similar increase in the mean size of Akita puncta per cell was also observed in LNPK KO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: RTN4 overexpression decreased the mean size of Akita puncta per cell in LNPK KO cells.
source: RTN4 overexpression also decreased the mean size of Akita puncta per cell in LNPK KO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: A decrease in the delivery of Akita to lysosomes was observed in LNPK KO and CLIMP63 overexpressing cells.
source: Consistent with the accumulation of large Akita puncta in the ER, a decrease in the delivery of Akita to lysosomes was observed in LNPK KO and CLIMP63 overexpressing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Akita puncta enlarge when ER sheets proliferate.
source: Together these findings indicate that Akita puncta enlarge when ER sheets proliferate.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: hCOL1A1 puncta did not show an increased accumulation in LNPK KO cells.
source: In contrast to what was observed for Akita, we did not see an increased accumulation of hCOL1A1 puncta in LNPK KO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: G57S Pro-AVP is a mutant neuropeptide whose expression leads to an autosomal-dominant neurodegenerative disorder called neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus (DI).
source: G57S Pro-AVP is a mutant neuropeptide whose expression leads to an autosomal-dominant neurodegenerative disorder called neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus (DI) (Spiess et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Spiess et al., 2020.

claim: C28F POMC is a mutant prohormone that causes early onset obesity.
source: C28F POMC is a mutant prohormone that causes early onset obesity (Kim et al., 2018; Creemers et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2018 and Creemers et al., 2008.

claim: Large puncta of G57S Pro-AVP accumulated in the siSEC24C, but not siSEC24A, depleted cells.
source: Like Akita, large puncta of G57S Pro-AVP accumulated in the siSEC24C, but not siSEC24A, depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Large G57S Pro-AVP puncta accumulation was more pronounced in LNPK KO cells.
source: Furthermore, large puncta accumulation was more pronounced in LNPKO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Similar results were obtained with C28F POMC.
source: Similar results were obtained with C28F POMC (Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F.

claim: A significant fraction (>30%) of the LNPK KO cells that contained G57S Pro-AVP contained multiple large puncta.
source: In addition, a significant fraction (>30%) of the LNPK KO cells that contained G57S Pro-AVP (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D) or C28F POMC (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F) contained multiple large puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3D.

claim: A significant fraction (>30%) of the LNPK KO cells that contained C28F POMC contained multiple large puncta.
source: In addition, a significant fraction (>30%) of the LNPK KO cells that contained G57S Pro-AVP (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D) or C28F POMC (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F) contained multiple large puncta.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Cargoes that are targeted for ER-phagy by the ER tubule receptor RTN3 form puncta that enlarge in sheet-like ER.
source: Together these studies have revealed that cargoes that are targeted for ER-phagy by the ER tubule receptor RTN3 form puncta that enlarge in sheet-like ER.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: A cargo that is targeted for ER-phagy by the ER sheets receptor, FAM134B, did not display the behavior of enlarging in sheets.
source: A cargo that is targeted for ER-phagy by the ER sheets receptor, FAM134B, did not display this behavior.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Akita is known to be cytotoxic in insulin-secreting β cells.
source: Akita is known to be cytotoxic in insulin-secreting β cells (Liu et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2007.

claim: Akita exerts a dominant-negative phenotype by trapping wild-type proinsulin in high-molecular-weight oligomeric complexes that are retained in the ER, thereby disrupting insulin secretion.
source: It exerts a dominant-negative phenotype by trapping wild-type proinsulin in high-molecular-weight oligomeric complexes that are retained in the ER, thereby disrupting insulin secretion (Liu et al., 2007; Izumi et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2007 and Izumi et al., 2003.

claim: When Akita-sfGFP and proinsulin-FLAG were co-transfected in control and LNPK KO cells, 100% of the large Akita puncta also contained proinsulin.
source: Interestingly, when Akita-sfGFP and proinsulin-FLAG were co-transfected in control and LNPK KO cells, 100% of the large Akita puncta also contained proinsulin (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: When G57S Pro-AVP-FLAG and Pro-AVP-HA were co-transfected, 100% of the large G57S Pro-AVP puncta also contained Pro-AVP.
source: The same was also observed when G57S Pro-AVP-FLAG and Pro-AVP-HA (Figure 5—figure supplement 4C and D), or C28F POMC and POMC-Myc (Figure 5—figure supplement 4E and F) were co-transfected.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4C and D.

claim: When C28F POMC and POMC-Myc were co-transfected, 100% of the large C28F POMC puncta also contained POMC.
source: The same was also observed when G57S Pro-AVP-FLAG and Pro-AVP-HA (Figure 5—figure supplement 4C and D), or C28F POMC and POMC-Myc (Figure 5—figure supplement 4E and F) were co-transfected.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4E and F.

claim: G57S Pro-AVP-FLAG and C28F POMC exert dominant-negative phenotypes.
source: Like Akita, G57S Pro-AVP-FLAG and C28F POMC exert dominant-negative phenotypes (Kim et al., 2018; Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2018 and Shi et al., 2017.

claim: Akita, G57S Pro-AVP, and C28F POMC behave similarly to the way they would in insulin-secreting or neuronal cells.
source: Together these findings suggest that Akita, G57S Pro-AVP, and C28F POMC behave similarly to the way they would in insulin-secreting or neuronal cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: The overexpression of CLIMP63 in insulin-secreting INS-1 832/13 rat β-cells (INS1) led to a significant increase in large Akita puncta.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5A–D.

claim: Images of 3D reconstructions of Z stacks suggested that the large Akita puncta reside in sheet-like ER in INS1 cells.
source: Images of 3D reconstructions of Z stacks suggested that the large Akita puncta reside in sheet-like ER (see representative images in Figure 5—figure supplement 5B, Video 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5B and Video 8.

claim: The LNPK KO cells contained the same number of SEC24C puncta as control cells.
source: Although the LNPK KO cells contained the same number of SEC24C puncta as control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and B), less Akita puncta colocalized with SEC24C (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and C), and fewer cells contained Akita puncta that colocalized with LC3B (Figure 5—figure supplement 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and B.

claim: Less Akita puncta colocalized with SEC24C in LNPK KO cells.
source: Although the LNPK KO cells contained the same number of SEC24C puncta as control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and B), less Akita puncta colocalized with SEC24C (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and C), and fewer cells contained Akita puncta that colocalized with LC3B (Figure 5—figure supplement 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and C.

claim: Fewer cells contained Akita puncta that colocalized with LC3B in LNPK KO cells.
source: Although the LNPK KO cells contained the same number of SEC24C puncta as control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and B), less Akita puncta colocalized with SEC24C (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A and C), and fewer cells contained Akita puncta that colocalized with LC3B (Figure 5—figure supplement 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6D and E.

claim: The reduction in ERPHS is consistent with the decreased delivery of Akita to lysosomes in LNPK KO cells.
source: The reduction in ERPHS is consistent with the decreased delivery of Akita to lysosomes in mutant cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Only the small Akita puncta (<0.12 µm2) associated with RTN3 puncta in control cells.
source: When we performed colocalization studies of Akita puncta with RTN3 puncta in control cells, only the small Akita puncta (<0.12 µm2) associated with RTN3 puncta (Figure 5D, top, and Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5E.

claim: Colocalizing Akita-RTN3 puncta were mostly detected at the tips and junctions of ER tubules.
source: Colocalizing puncta were mostly detected at the tips and junctions of ER tubules (arrowheads, Figure 5D, top), and also observed when autophagosome formation was blocked (Figure 5—figure supplement 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 7A.

claim: The diffuse pool of Akita in the ER network colocalized with the pan ER marker SEC61 in the network.
source: Although the diffuse pool of Akita in the ER network colocalized with the pan ER marker SEC61 in the network, the SEC61 puncta that formed on the ER did not colocalize with Akita puncta (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: The SEC61 puncta that formed on the ER did not colocalize with Akita puncta.
source: Although the diffuse pool of Akita in the ER network colocalized with the pan ER marker SEC61 in the network, the SEC61 puncta that formed on the ER did not colocalize with Akita puncta (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: The colocalization of small Akita puncta with RTN3 puncta was specific.
source: Thus, the colocalization of small Akita puncta with RTN3 puncta was specific.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the comparison with SEC61.

claim: Akita puncta did not colocalize with RTN3 puncta in LNPK KO cells.
source: In contrast to control cells, Akita puncta did not colocalize with RTN3 puncta in LNPK KO cells (Figure 5D and E, bottom).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Large Akita puncta were largely seen in sheet-like dense regions of the ER in LNPK KO cells, while RTN3 was frequently seen at the cell periphery.
source: Large Akita puncta (arrows) were largely seen in sheet-like dense regions of the ER, while RTN3 was frequently seen at the cell periphery in the KO cells (Figure 5D, bottom).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The inability of small Akita puncta to colocalize with RTN3 puncta in LNPK KO cells was not a consequence of decreased puncta movement in the network.
source: The inability of small Akita puncta to colocalize with RTN3 puncta in LNPK KO cells was not a consequence of decreased puncta movement in the network as the velocity of the small puncta was not significantly altered in mutant cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 7B.

claim: The large Akita puncta in LNPK KO cells did not colocalize with SEC61 puncta, but were frequently seen in the ER lumen.
source: The large Akita puncta in LNPK KO cells also did not colocalize with SEC61 puncta, but were frequently seen in the ER lumen (Figure 5—figure supplement 7C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 7C and D.

claim: FRAP analysis of the large puncta revealed that Akita-sfGFP in the puncta rapidly exchanged with the Akita-sfGFP in the network of LNPK KO cells.
source: FRAP analysis of the large puncta revealed that Akita-sfGFP in the puncta rapidly exchanged with the Akita-sfGFP in the network of mutant cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 8A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 8A–D.

claim: The Akita-sfGFP in the large puncta rapidly exchanged with the ER network pool in siRTN3-depleted cells.
source: The Akita-sfGFP in the large puncta also rapidly exchanged with the ER network pool in siRTN3-depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 9A–D), indicating that Akita did not aggregate in the absence of RTN3.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 9A–D.

claim: Akita did not aggregate in the absence of RTN3.
source: The Akita-sfGFP in the large puncta also rapidly exchanged with the ER network pool in siRTN3-depleted cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 9A–D), indicating that Akita did not aggregate in the absence of RTN3.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the FRAP data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 9A–D.

claim: The failure of Akita to access RTN3 in LNPK KO cells is a consequence of its exclusion from tubules.
source: Together these findings imply that the failure of Akita to access RTN3 in LNPK KO cells is a consequence of its exclusion from tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Overexpressed RTN3 increases the density of three-way ER junctions.
source: Overexpressed RTN3 increases the density of three-way ER junctions, while RTN4 drives ER tubulation (Wang et al., 2016; Wu and Voeltz, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2016 and Wu and Voeltz, 2021.

claim: RTN4 drives ER tubulation.
source: Overexpressed RTN3 increases the density of three-way ER junctions, while RTN4 drives ER tubulation (Wang et al., 2016; Wu and Voeltz, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2016 and Wu and Voeltz, 2021.

claim: RTN4 does not associate with LC3B or other Atg8 family members.
source: Unlike RTN3, RTN4 does not associate with LC3B or other Atg8 family members (Grumati et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Grumati et al., 2017.

claim: The loss of LNPK does not reduce the level of RTN4.
source: Consistent with previous studies showing that the loss of LNPK does not reduce the level of RTN4 (Wang et al., 2016), we found that RTN3 levels were also unaltered in the KO cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2016.

claim: RTN3 levels were unaltered in the LNPK KO cells.
source: Consistent with previous studies showing that the loss of LNPK does not reduce the level of RTN4 (Wang et al., 2016), we found that RTN3 levels were also unaltered in the KO cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The sheet-like ER was partially converted to ER tubules in LNPK KO cells transfected with either RTN3 or RTN4.
source: The sheet-like ER was partially converted to ER tubules in LNPK KO cells transfected with either RTN3 or RTN4 (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: As the number of cells with sheet-like ER decreased, the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta decreased.
source: As the number of cells with sheet-like ER decreased, the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta decreased (Figure 6C,D), and small Akita puncta became more visible in the ER tubules (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Small Akita puncta became more visible in the ER tubules when the number of cells with sheet-like ER decreased.
source: As the number of cells with sheet-like ER decreased, the percentage of cells with large Akita puncta decreased (Figure 6C,D), and small Akita puncta became more visible in the ER tubules (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The overexpression of RTN3 or RTN4 reduced the number of large Akita puncta equally as well.
source: The overexpression of RTN3 or RTN4 reduced the number of large Akita puncta equally as well, indicating that the reduction in large puncta was driven by the formation of tubules.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The reduction in large Akita puncta was driven by the formation of tubules.
source: The overexpression of RTN3 or RTN4 reduced the number of large Akita puncta equally as well, indicating that the reduction in large puncta was driven by the formation of tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: More Akita was delivered to lysosomes when sheet-like ER was converted to tubules in LNPK KO cells transfected with RTN3 or RTN4.
source: When we transfected KO cells with Akita-sfGFP and either mTurquoise2-RTN3 or mTurquoise2-RTN4, we found that more Akita was delivered to lysosomes when sheet-like ER was converted to tubules (Figure 6E and F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E and F, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Akita can only be targeted to ER-phagy in tubules.
source: Together these findings indicate that Akita can only be targeted to ER-phagy in tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: In the absence of tubules, Akita puncta enlarge in sheets.
source: In the absence of tubules, Akita puncta enlarge in sheets.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.
